newsitem.title: ITALY: Prodi says Kohl backs rapid Italy path to EMU.
newsitem.headline: Prodi says Kohl backs rapid Italy path to EMU.

text.p: Italy said on Friday it had German support for "rapid, effective" progress towards membership of Europe's planned single currency and confirmed that Rome would seek re-entry to the exchange rate mechanism by year end.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi, who met Chancellor Helmut Kohl in Bonn on Thursday night, told reporters Kohl had told him he hoped Italy would make "rapid, effective" progress towards joining the single currency at its start in 1999.

Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi, speaking with Prodi, confirmed Italy's intention to ask its partners to return the lira to the ERM before the end of 1996. The currency crashed out of the grid in 1992.

Ciampi said the precise timetable was linked to passage through parliament of Italy's 1997 budget and that the re-entry rate should reflect the lira's level against other leading currencies in the preceding "weeks, months".
Italy has drawn up a tough 1997 budget to try to meet the criteria for economic and monetary union.

Prodi, who was speaking after the inaugural session of an Italian committee on the introduction of the euro single currency, said in a speech to the session that no country could allow itself to miss membership of EMU from the start.
